title: Does shallow alignment manifest differently in chain-of-thought vs. direct-answer models?

original_idea.problem: Whether shallow alignment applies in the same way to reasoning models which may refuse inside the chain-of-thought is untested.
original_idea.direction: Measure alignment depth using KL curves in both direct-answer and CoT modes. Test whether prefilling attacks are effective when the model reasons first.
original_idea.why_it_matters: If CoT naturally deepens alignment, it could be a no-cost improvement. If attacks target reasoning segments, a new attack surface is exposed.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: CoT modifies first-token dynamics -> may deepen or expose new alignment surface -> directly relevant as reasoning models become dominant. Addresses an important emerging threat model.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires KL divergence computation in two modes and understanding of CoT prompting. Intermediate complexity. CoT prompting is easy but comparing depth profiles requires solid understanding.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Deliverable requires sustained effort: running both modes, computing depth in each, testing attacks in each. Multiple experimental conditions before a clean comparison.

novelty.reasoning: This is now substantially addressed by the Chain-of-Thought Hijacking paper (arXiv:2510.26418, ICML 2025 submission) which demonstrates that refusal relies on a fragile, low-dimensional safety signal that becomes diluted as reasoning grows longer. The paper shows mechanistically that mid layers encode safety checking strength while late layers encode verification outcome, and long benign CoT dilutes both signals. CoT Hijacking achieves 94-100% ASR on reasoning models. H-CoT (arXiv:2502.12893) further confirms this for OpenAI o1/o3, DeepSeek-R1. RECAP (2026) proposes a defense. The core question — whether CoT deepens or weakens alignment — is answered: CoT weakens alignment by diluting safety signals, and attacks specifically targeting the reasoning chain are highly effective.
